newsitem.title: USA: GM reaches pact to end Janesville, Wis. strike.
newsitem.headline: GM reaches pact to end Janesville, Wis. strike.

text.p: General Motors Corp. said Tuesday it reached a tentative agreement with United Auto Workers union Local 95 to end a week-old strike at its Janesville, Wis., truck plant.

GM spokesman Thomas Beamon said Janesville's 4,809 UAW workers were scheduled to vote on the new local agreement at about 1 p.m. EST Wednesday. Production of Chevrolet and GMC full-size sport utility vehicles at the plant would resume shortly after the vote if the deal is ratified.

Neither GM nor officials for Local 95 would discuss details of the agreement. The union's members walked off the job Oct. 29 over plant-specific issues, including demands for more jobs to ease heavy overtime and an increasing workload.

"We're confident we've got a fair and equitable agreement for our membership," said Buford Beleau, a spokesman for Local 95 in Janesville. "We just want to get back to work building trucks and provide for our families, like everybody else."

The Janesville walkout was one of two local strikes that erupted last week as GM's national contract negotiations with the UAW heated up. About 2,750 workers at the automaker's Indianapolis metal stamping plant returned to work on Sunday after GM agreed to hire 200 new workers and drop demands to change skilled trade job classifications.
